reason: This passage (from Nehemiah 4) depicts the Hebrew people suffering from external threats and the difficult labor of rebuilding Jerusalem's walls. However, when the people become discouraged, expressing that 'the strength of the laborers has collapsed and there is too much rubble' (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָ֗ה כָּשַׁל֙ כֹּ֣חַ הַסַּבָּ֔ל), Nehemiah the leader responds with encouragement, not blame. He tells them 'Do not be afraid of them; remember the Lord who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your houses' (אַל־ תִּֽירְא֖וּ...אֶת־ אֲדֹנָ֞י הַגָּד֤וֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא֙). The leaders rally the people to action and courage rather than attributing their suffering to their own fault.
